A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CapMAS research. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and matchable, including the relocation of Prompt Templates from Appendix F to G.

before.justification: v1 reports original hallucination-detection experiments, human-alignment evaluations, captioning comparisons, ablations and bias analyses.

after.justification: v3 retains these empirical results and adds SPARC comparison results, fluency evaluations and GPT-4V Self-Refine experiments.

M1.justification: Section 3.2 retains the same LLM decomposition, independent MLLM proposition checking, thresholding and LLM caption correction. Appendix F's inference-time scaling discussion does not introduce a changed CapMAS procedure.

E1.justification: The IIW-400/DOCCI captioning coverage, DCI validation data and VQA benchmark coverage are retained. The new fluency and Self-Refine analyses remain within detailed image captioning, with no new dataset, domain or task coverage reported.

E2.justification: Table 5 adds SPARC while retaining VCD, OPERA, LURE, Volcano and LRV. Table 10 introduces human captions as fluency comparators, and Table 11 separately evaluates Self-Refine against unrefined GPT-4V captions.

E3.justification: Appendix F introduces GPT-4o fluency scoring on a 0–100 scale and GPT-4V Self-Refine evaluation at one, two and three iterations. These are additional evaluation procedures; previously stated experimental settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix F adds two focused supplementary analyses: CapMAS output fluency relative to human captions and caption-quality sensitivity to Self-Refine iterations. The existing threshold ablation, stylistic-bias analysis and caption case study are retained.

E5.justification: Figure 2's mean and standard-deviation reporting and Section 3.1's 40 stochastic caption generations are unchanged. The added results introduce no new seed information, uncertainty estimates or significance tests.

E6.justification: Existing numerical entries are unchanged. Additions include SPARC's 64.7 CLAIR, 50.2 factuality and 44.9 coverage in Table 5; GPT-4o fluency scores of 93.4–94.1 for CapMAS versus 89.0 for human captions in Table 10; and factuality declining from 77.1 to 69.8 after three Self-Refine iterations in Table 11.

T1.justification: The hallucination-score formula in Equation (1), threshold definitions and factuality ratio are unchanged. No mathematical assumption, theorem, proof or derivation is added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same CapMAS, dual-evaluation and benchmark contributions, factuality-improvement claims including GPT-4V, and concerns about VQA-centric assessment.

C2.justification: Appendix F newly attributes fluency to the corrector, interprets CapMAS as inference-time scaling and argues for a favorable cost-performance relationship with Self-Refine. Section 4.4 also discusses SPARC's coverage benefit. The efficiency argument is qualitative, without measured runtime or compute comparisons.

D1.justification: The abstract newly states code/data availability and provides a repository link. Appendix F supplies the exact GPT-4o fluency and GPT-4V Self-Refine prompts, adding reproducibility information for the new analyses.

R1.justification: v3 adds Jung et al. (2025, SPARC) and Madaan et al. (2023, Self-Refine), connecting them to additional comparisons and inference-time scaling. The existing related-work discussion and principal novelty positioning remain substantially unchanged.

P1.justification: v3 inserts Additional Experiments as Appendix F, moves Prompt Templates to G and updates cross-references. It also adds acknowledgements, publication information and the abstract resource link, and removes the draft template header. Most existing prose is unchanged.

P2.justification: v3 adds Tables 10–11, extends Table 5 with a SPARC row and reflows references and appendix material, including the prompt figures. Existing figure graphics and the other table designs are retained.

improvement.justification: v3 modestly strengthens empirical scrutiny through SPARC and the fluency/Self-Refine studies, while adding prompts and code/data access information. These are useful but limited gains: fluency is model-judged without comparison to uncorrected captions, and the claimed cost advantage lacks runtime or compute measurements. The central method and existing evidence remain unchanged.
